artworks.title: Biblis
artworks.description: Bouguereau's Academic nude presents Ovid's Carian twin collapsed beside the spring she will become — Byblis after the letter, the pursuit, and the tears that dissolve her into water.

artworks.title: Byblis Turning into a Spring
artworks.description: Henner paints the metamorphosis mid-flow: Byblis' body softens into the fountain that will bear her name — the Miletus daughter's incestuous grief made liquid.

artworks.title: Biblis Changed into a Spring
artworks.description: Point's Symbolist panel returns to the same Ovidian close: Byblis as a fountain-nymph, the rejected twin whose tears become a permanent spring in Caria.

artworks.title: Biblis
artworks.description: Collin's reclining Byblis belongs to the Third Republic taste for Ovidian nudes — the sister of Caunus rendered as a languid study in forbidden desire and exhaustion.

artworks.title: Byblis Loves Her Brother
artworks.description: Solis' woodcut for the Metamorphoses shows Byblis writing or pursuing Caunus — the Renaissance print tradition that fixed her letter and chase as a standard Ovid plate.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Ovid's Byblis writes, pursues, and weeps herself into a spring — the Carian twin whose letter became a set-piece of forbidden desire.

popCulture.title: Byblis
popCulture.description: Daughter of Miletus who loved her twin Caunus — aetiology of a spring and a caution still filed under her name.

popCulture.title: Parthenius of Nicaea
popCulture.creator: Parthenius
popCulture.description: Love Romances preserves the Hellenistic Byblis variants — the dossier Ovid amplified into metamorphosis.
